tips.title: Use Standard Headings
tips.description: Use standard section headings like 'Work Experience', 'Education', and 'Skills'. ATS systems are programmed to recognize these specific headings.

tips.title: Avoid Graphics & Tables
tips.description: Stick to simple text formatting. Complex graphics, tables, and text boxes can confuse ATS parsers and cause your information to be missed.

tips.title: Include Relevant Keywords
tips.description: Carefully read the job description and include exact keywords and phrases. Match the language used in the job posting.

tips.title: Save as PDF/DOCX
tips.description: Always save your resume as a PDF or DOCX file. These formats preserve formatting and are most compatible with ATS systems.

tips.title: Use a Simple Layout
tips.description: Avoid columns, complex formatting, and unusual fonts. A simple, clean layout ensures maximum ATS compatibility.

tips.title: Include a Skills Section
tips.description: Create a dedicated skills section listing your technical and soft skills. This is often the first section ATS scans.

tips.title: Use Action Verbs
tips.description: Start bullet points with strong action verbs like 'Led', 'Developed', 'Implemented', 'Achieved' to make your accomplishments stand out.

tips.title: Quantify Achievements
tips.description: Use numbers and metrics to demonstrate your impact. For example: 'Increased sales by 40%' or 'Managed team of 15 people'.

tips.title: Customize for Each Job
tips.description: Tailor your resume for each application. Match keywords and requirements from the specific job description.

tips.title: Keep Formatting Simple
tips.description: Use standard fonts like Arial, Calibri, or Times New Roman. Avoid fancy fonts, underlines, and italics.
